title: Dimension of local components under weakly etale maps from a universally catenary domain
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], universally catenary in the sense of [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Let $K$ be its fraction field, and suppose that the integral closure $\overline C$ of $C$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $C$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring, and let $f:C\to D$ be a local weakly etale homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], where local means $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_D)=\mathfrak m_C$. For every minimal prime ideal $P$ of $D$, one has $\dim(D/P)=\dim C$, with Krull dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. A minimal prime is a prime containing no strictly smaller prime. A local ring has exactly one maximal ideal, and a domain is nonzero and has no zero divisors.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings, Nagoya Math. J. 60 (1976), 139–149
source.place: Lemma 5.5, printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9); standing Noetherian convention from the introduction and Remark 5.2.

proof.text: Fix a minimal prime $P$ of $D$ and put $C'=\overline C^{\,K}$. Apply [lem-exc-weakly-etale-normalization-tensor]; its Noetherian, local, domain, universal-catenarity, finite-normalization and weak-etaleness hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses here. Thus $D$ is reduced and $D'=C'\otimes_C D\cong E\times F$ as $D$-algebras, with $E$ the integral closure of $A=D/P$ in its fraction field. The quotient $A$ is a Noetherian local domain: ideals lift to finitely generated ideals of $D$, primes lift to primes containing $P$, and its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_D/P$. If $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ generate $C'$ over $C$, then $c_i\otimes1$ generate $D'$ over $D$, since $c\otimes d=\sum_i(c_i\otimes1)f(a_i)d$ for $c=\sum_i a_ic_i$. Their images generate $E$ over $A$, because $P$ acts by zero in the specified projection. In particular $E$ is finite over $A$.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), Lemma 5.5 proof
source.place: Printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9), normalization, choice of n, local AF dimension equality, and universally catenary normalization dimension.

proof.text: The inclusion $A\hookrightarrow E$ is integral by the definition of integral closure. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal] gives $\dim E=\dim A=d$, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-finite-krull-dimension] makes $d$ a finite nonnegative integer. By the definition of dimension a chain of length $d$ in $E$ exists. Using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ containing its last prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], that chain gives $\dim E_{\mathfrak n}\ge d$, and every chain below $\mathfrak n$ is a chain of $E$, giving the reverse bound. Thus $\dim E_{\mathfrak n}=\dim A$. This uses no catenarity assertion about $A$.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), Lemma 5.5 proof
source.place: Printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9), normalization, choice of n, local AF dimension equality, and universally catenary normalization dimension.

proof.text: Base change of $C\to D$ gives the weakly etale map $C'\to C'\otimes_C D=D'$ by [lem-exc-weakly-etale-ring-base-change-composition]. In the product $E\times F$, the projection to $E$ is localization at the idempotent $e=(1,0)$: after $e$ is inverted it becomes $1$, so every $(0,b)=(1-e)(0,b)$ becomes zero, and $(a,0)\mapsto a$ supplies the inverse isomorphism. Thus the projection is weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-ring-weakly-etale]. Composition and localization at $\mathfrak n$ give a weakly etale map $h:C'\to E_{\mathfrak n}$. Let $\mathfrak m$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak n$ in $C'$. The map $h$ inverts $C'\setminus\mathfrak m$. Its base change to $C'_{\mathfrak m}$ identifies with $g:C'_{\mathfrak m}\to E_{\mathfrak n}$: the isomorphism sends $(a/s)\otimes b$ to $h(a)h(s)^{-1}b$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Consequently $g$ is weakly etale and local; a fraction $a/s$ maps into the maximal ideal precisely when $a\in\mathfrak m$. No locality of $C'\to E$ is asserted.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), Lemma 5.5 proof
source.place: Printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9), normalization, choice of n, local AF dimension equality, and universally catenary normalization dimension.

proof.text: Since $E$ is finite over the local ring $A$ by step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical] gives $\mathfrak n\cap A=\mathfrak m_A$. Therefore $\mathfrak m\cap C=\mathfrak m_C$, using $\mathfrak n\cap D=\mathfrak m_D$ and the locality of $C\to D$. The finite map $C\to C'$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Any prime properly containing $\mathfrak m$ would still contract to the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_C$, contradicting [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability]; [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] supplies a maximal ideal containing $\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak m$ is maximal. The finite-normalization dimension theorem [lem-exc-weakly-etale-normalization-dimension] now applies to $C$ and this $\mathfrak m$, and gives $\dim C'_{\mathfrak m}=\dim C$.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), Lemma 5.5 proof
source.place: Printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9), normalization, choice of n, local AF dimension equality, and universally catenary normalization dimension.

proof.text: Write $R=C'_{\mathfrak m}$ and $S=E_{\mathfrak n}$. By the definition of weak etaleness, the local map $g:R\to S$ is flat. Therefore [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective] makes it faithfully flat, and [lem-sc-faithfully-flat-local-dimension] gives $\dim R\le\dim S$.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), Lemma 5.5 proof
source.place: Printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9), normalization, choice of n, local AF dimension equality, and universally catenary normalization dimension.

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, the fibre $H=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is weakly etale over the field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by [lem-exc-weakly-etale-ring-base-change-composition]. Every singly generated subalgebra of $H$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field], so the finite-algebra integrality lemma [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] makes every element integral over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. All primes of $H$ contract to $(0)$ in that field; hence [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] makes them incomparable. The inclusion-preserving fibre-prime bijection [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] consequently forbids two comparable distinct primes of $S$ with the same contraction to $R$. Contracting a strict chain in $S$ therefore gives a strict chain of the same length in $R$, so $\dim S\le\dim R$.

source.document: Silvio Greco, Two theorems on excellent rings (1976), Lemma 5.5 proof
source.place: Printed p. 147 (PDF p. 9), normalization, choice of n, local AF dimension equality, and universally catenary normalization dimension.

proof.text: Steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 give $\dim(D/P)=\dim E_{\mathfrak n}=\dim C'_{\mathfrak m}=\dim C$. This proves the claim for the arbitrary minimal prime $P$. For $\dim C=0$ every equality is still valid. A ring with no minimal prime contributes no instance of the universally quantified conclusion.

Step 2: dim E_n = dim A, using integral-injective dimension, finite local dimension, maximal ideal existence and chains-below-prime; no catenarity of A is used. Step 4: n∩A = m_A, so m∩C = m_C, and m is maximal by incomparability. Step 5: flat local map, so faithfully flat, so dim R <= dim S. Step 6: the fibre over a field is weakly étale with integral elements (092Q), so fibre primes are incomparable and the inclusion-preserving fibre bijection gives dim S <= dim R. Step 7 is elementary.
